# iliad-116 — renderings chosen for the Iliad (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| νεῶν ὀρθοκραιράων (18.3, of ships) | "the ships, straight-horned" | "the straight-horned ships" (+ note: what the "horns" of a ship are is not known) | "high-prowed", "upright-prowed", "tall-sterned" (each decides the reading); extends the Odyssey row ὀρθοκραίρων βοῶν "straight-horned cattle" to ships without choosing a referent |
| ὤ μοι ἐγώ (18.6) | "Oh me" | "Oh me" | "Alas", "Woe is me"; follows the table's ὤ μοι ἐγών (16.433, 17.91), ἐγώ unrendered |
| μὴ … τελέσωσι θεοὶ κακὰ κήδεα θυμῷ (18.8, fear clause) | "lest now the gods fulfil for me evil sorrows in my heart" | "I fear the gods may now fulfil evil sorrows for my heart" | "bring to pass" (kept for the perfect τετέλεσται, 18.74); τελέω keeps "fulfil" here, "accomplish" in τετελεσμένα (18.4) and τετέλεσται (18.74), "bring to completion" for ἐξετέλεσσεν (18.79); κακὰ κήδεα "evil sorrows" is the table's 6.165 row |
| ὥς ποτέ μοι μήτηρ διεπέφραδε καί μοι ἔειπε (18.9) | "as once my mother made plain to me and told me" | "as my mother once made plain to me and told me" | "revealed", "foretold", "prophesied" (each makes the warning a prophecy; the Greek says only "make plain" and "tell"); διαφράζω "make plain" |
| φάος ἠελίοιο (18.11, 18.61) | "the light of the sun" | "the light of the sun" | "sunlight" alone; the table's λαμπρὸν φάος ἠελίοιο "the bright light of the sun" without λαμπρόν |
| σχέτλιος (18.13, of Patroclus) | "cruel one" | "the cruel one" (+ note: the word is "hard, unyielding"; here reproach and grief together) | "headstrong", "stubborn", "reckless" (each decides the tone); keeps the table's σχέτλιος "cruel one" |
| ἂψ ἐπὶ νῆας ἴμεν (18.14) | "back to the ships to go" | "to go back to the ships" | "retreat", "withdraw" |
| ἀγαυοῦ Νέστορος υἱός (18.16, Antilochus unnamed) | "the son of noble Nestor" | "the son of noble Nestor" | "Antilochus" (the poet does not name him here), "Nestor's brave son"; ἀγαυός keeps "noble" (the table's 3.268 row) |
| ὤφελλε γενέσθαι with μή (18.19) | "which, would that it had not come to be" | "if only it had not happened" | "which should never have been", "that ought never to have been" (state a duty the Greek does not state); follows the table's αἴθ’ ὄφελες "If only" |
| τὸν δ’ ἄχεος νεφέλη ἐκάλυψε μέλαινα (18.22; shared with 17.591, iliad-114) | "and him a cloud of grief covered, dark" | "a dark cloud of grief covered Achilles" | "a black cloud of sorrow" (the published `i` of 17.591 says "dark cloud of grief"; kept); the name Achilles is supplied in `i` as Hector was at 17.591 |
| χαρίεν … πρόσωπον (18.24) | "graceful face" | "graceful face" | "handsome", "lovely", "fair"; χαρίεις "graceful" as in the table's χαρίεντα εἵματα |
| ᾔσχυνε (18.24, 18.27) | "disfigured" | "disfigured" | "defiled", "marred", "shamed"; αἰσχύνω "disfigure" of face and of hair, one word each time |
| νεκταρέῳ χιτῶνι (18.25) | "nectar-sweet tunic" | "tunic, sweet as nectar" | follows the table's νεκταρέου ἑανοῦ (3.385) "nectar-sweet robe" / "robe, sweet as nectar"; "nectarous", "fragrant" avoided as there |
| μέγας μεγαλωστὶ τανυσθείς (18.26, of Achilles living) | "great in his greatness, stretched out" | "stretched out at full length" | "stretched his great length", "huge in his hugeness"; follows the table's 16.775–776 row; τανυσθείς "stretched out" |
| δμῳαί (18.28) | "maidservants" | "maidservants" | "slave-women", "handmaids"; the table's 6.375 "maidservants/maids" |
| ληΐσσατο (18.28) | "took as spoil" | "had taken as spoil" | "plundered", "carried off" |
| θυμὸν ἀκηχέμεναι (18.29) | "sorrowing at heart" | "grieved at heart" | "mourning", "pained"; follows ἀκηχέδατ’ "are grieved" (17.637) |
| χερσὶ … στήθεα πεπλήγοντο (18.30–31; also 18.50–51) | "with their hands … beat their breasts" | "beat their breasts with their hands" | "smote", "struck their chests"; one rendering at both places |
| λύθεν δ’ ὑπὸ γυῖα ἑκάστης (18.31) | "loosed beneath were the limbs of each" | "the limbs of each gave way beneath her" | "their knees were loosed" (the Greek says γυῖα "limbs"), "weakened"; the idiom λῦσε γυῖα "loosed his limbs" (4.469) is kept for killing, this use is of grief |
| ὀδύρετο δάκρυα λείβων (18.32) | "lamented, tears pouring" | "lamented, pouring out his tears" | "wept", "wailed"; follows the table's ὀδύρομαι "lament" and δάκρυα λείβων "pouring out his tears" (5.84) |
| κυδάλιμον κῆρ (18.33) | "glorious heart" | "glorious heart" | the table's 12.45 row unchanged |
| δείδιε … μὴ λαιμὸν ἀπαμήσειε σιδήρῳ (18.34) | "he feared lest he cut his throat with iron" | "Antilochus feared that Achilles would cut his own throat with the iron" | "slit", "sever" (each decides the depth of the cut); ἀπαμάω "cut through"; σίδηρος "iron" as in the table's 4.123 row; names supplied in `i` because the Greek leaves both subjects unnamed |
| σμερδαλέον δ’ ᾤμωξεν (18.35) | "terribly he wailed" | "he cried out terribly" | "groaned" (kept for στενάχω), "shrieked"; follows ᾤμωξεν (3.364) and σμερδαλέα ἰάχων "crying out terribly" (5.302) |
| κώκυσεν · κωκύσασα (18.37, 18.71) | "cried out" · "having cried out" | "cried out" · "with a shrill cry" | "shrieked", "wailed" (kept for οἰμώζω); the Odyssey's κώκυσεν "cried out" (odyssey-008); ὀξύ "shrilly" is new |
| θεαὶ … Νηρηΐδες (18.37–38, 18.49) | "the goddesses … Nereids" | "the goddesses … Nereids" | "sea-nymphs", "daughters of Nereus" (the Greek names them Nereids only); the familiar Latin form |
| the Nereids' names (18.39–49) | Glauce, Thaleia, Cymodoce, Nesaea, Speio, Thoe, Halia, Cymothoe, Actaea, Limnoreia, Melite, Iaera, Amphithoe, Agave, Doto, Proto, Pherusa, Dynamene, Dexamene, Amphinome, Callianeira, Doris, Panope, Galatea, Nemertes, Apseudes, Callianassa, Clymene, Ianeira, Ianassa, Maera, Oreithyia, Amatheia | same | "Glauke", "Kymodoke" and other transliterated endings; the Latinised forms as in the Odyssey table's Phaeacian names; the meanings that can be read go in the notes, once |
| βοῶπις (Ἁλίη βοῶπις, 18.40) | "ox-eyed Halia" | "ox-eyed Halia" | the table's βοῶπις "ox-eyed" (1.551) |
| ἀγακλειτὴ Γαλάτεια (18.45) | "renowned Galatea" | "renowned Galatea" | "famous", "glorious"; follows ἀγακλειτός "renowned" (16.463) |
| ἐϋπλόκαμος Ἀμάθεια (18.48) | "fine-plaited Amatheia" | "fine-plaited Amatheia" | the table's ἐϋπλόκαμος "fine-plaited" (6.380, 11.624) |
| ἀργύφεον σπέος (18.50) | "silver-white cave" | "silver-white cave" | "silvery", "gleaming"; follows ἀργύφεον φᾶρος "silver-white robe" (10.543) |
| Θέτις δ’ ἐξῆρχε γόοιο (18.51) | "Thetis led off the lament" | "Thetis led off the lament" | "began the wailing", "led the dirge" (ἐξάρχω "lead off" with the genitive, kept apart from ἐξῆρχε "led the way out" at 2.84; γόος "lament") |
| κλῦτε κασίγνηται Νηρηΐδες (18.52) | "Hear, sister Nereids" | "Hear me, sister Nereids" | "Listen", "Hear my words"; follows κλῦτε φίλοι (2.56) "Hear, friends" / "Hear me, friends"; κασίγνητος "sister" is the feminine of the table's "brother" |
| ὤ μοι ἐγὼ δειλή (18.54) | "Oh me, miserable that I am" | "Oh me, miserable that I am" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "poor"; δειλός "miserable" (the table's 5.574 and 11.816 rows) |
| δυσαριστοτόκεια (18.54, hapax) | "ill-fated mother of the best" | "unhappy mother of the best" | "mother of the best, ill-starred", "bearer of the best in sorrow" (each reorders the parts); sense read from δυσ- + ἄριστος + τόκος, the note says the word occurs only here |
| ἔξοχον ἡρώων (18.56) | "standing out above the heroes" | "standing out above the heroes" | "outstanding", "pre-eminent" (reserved); follows ἔξοχον ἡρώεσσιν "standing out" (2.483) and ἔξοχον ἄλλων "above all others" (9.631) |
| ἔρνεϊ ἶσος (18.56) | "equal to a sapling" | "like a young sapling" | the Odyssey row ἔρνεϊ ἶσον (14.175) unchanged; ἀνέδραμεν "ran up" in `l`, "sprang up" in `i` |
| γουνῷ ἀλωῆς (18.57) | "on the rich ground of an orchard" | "on the rich ground of an orchard" | the table's 9.534 row unchanged, with the article changed to "an" (the note says the sense of γουνός is not certain) |
| νηυσὶν ἐπιπροέηκα κορωνίσιν Ἴλιον εἴσω (18.58) | "sent forth upon the curved ships into Ilium" | "sent him forth in the curved ships to Ilium" | "hollow ships" (reserved for κοῖλος), "beaked"; κορωνίς "curved" (19.182 row); Ἴλιον "Ilium" as in Book 1's Ἴλιος ἱρή "sacred Ilium" |
| τὸν δ’ οὐχ ὑποδέξομαι αὖτις οἴκαδε νοστήσαντα (18.59–60; again, in the second person, 18.89–90) | "I shall not receive him again returned home" · "whom you will not receive again returned home" | "I shall not receive him back again, returned home" · "you will not receive back again, returned home" | "welcome", "greet", "take in" (ὑποδέχομαι "receive"); the same English in both mouths, since Achilles hands her words back to her |
| χραισμῆσαι (18.62) | "help" | "help" | "avail" (kept for the sense "ward off"), "save"; follows χραισμέω "ward off / help" (7.144) |
| ὄφρα ἴδωμι φίλον τέκος (18.63) | "that I may see my dear child" | "to see my dear child" | "my beloved son"; τέκος "child" as in the table's τέκνον "child" (1.362), not "son" |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα λίπε σπέος (18.65) | "So then, having spoken, she left the cave" | "With these words she left the cave" | "she spoke and departed"; follows ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπεβήσετο (2.35) "With these words he went away" |
| περὶ δέ σφισι κῦμα θαλάσσης ῥήγνυτο (18.66–67) | "around them the wave of the sea was breaking" | "the wave of the sea broke about them" | "parted for them", "opened a path" (the Greek does not say it opened) |
| ἐπισχερώ (18.68) | "one after another" | "one after another" | the table's 11.668 row unchanged ("in a row" in the former `l`; here `l` takes the `i` wording) |
| θαμειαί (νέες, 18.68) | "thick-set" | "lay drawn up close together" | "crowded", "in dense array"; εἴρυντο from ἐρύω "draw up" (the note names the verb, apart from ἐρύομαι "guard") |
| ὀξὺ δὲ κωκύσασα κάρη λάβε παιδὸς ἑοῖο (18.71) | "having cried out shrilly she took hold of the head of her own child" | "with a shrill cry she took hold of her child's head" | "clasped his head", "took his head in her hands" (adds a gesture the Greek leaves open); παῖς "child" |
| ἐξαύδα, μὴ κεῦθε (18.74) | "Speak out, do not hide it" | "Speak it out, do not keep it hidden" | the published 1.363 wording, shortened by the missing νόῳ |
| ἀεκήλια ἔργα (18.77, rare) | "unwelcome deeds" | "unwelcome deeds" (+ note: exact sense uncertain; compare ἀέκων "unwilling") | "unseemly" (reserved for ἀεικής), "unfitting", "grievous" (reserved for ἀλεγεινός and λυγρός), "shameful" |
| τὰ μὲν ἄρ μοι Ὀλύμπιος ἐξετέλεσσεν (18.79) | "those things indeed the Olympian has brought to completion for me" | "the Olympian has brought those things to pass for me" | "Zeus" (the name is withheld), "fulfilled"; follows the table's Ὀλύμπιος "the Olympian" (2.309) |
| ἦδος (18.80) | "pleasure" | "pleasure" (+ note: exact sense uncertain) | "joy", "enjoyment"; follows the table's ἦδος (11.317) |
| τὸν ἐγὼ περὶ πάντων τῖον ἑταίρων ἶσον ἐμῇ κεφαλῇ (18.81–82) | "whom I honoured above all companions equally with my own head" | "whom I honoured above all my companions, as much as my own head" (+ note: the head stands for the self) | "as myself", "as my own life" (each decides what κεφαλή stands for), "as my very soul"; ἶσον "equally" with the dative (9.142 row); τίω "honour" |
| τεύχεα … πελώρια θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι καλά (18.82–84) | "armour … huge, a wonder to behold, fine" | "armour, huge, a wonder to look at, and fine" | "monstrous", "marvellous"; follows τεύχεα χρύσεια πελώρια θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι (10.439) "huge, a wonder to behold" / "huge, a wonder to look at" |
| δῃώσας (18.83) | "having cut him down" | "cut him down" | "slain", "slaughtered"; δηϊόω "cut down", as in the table's δῄουν "hacked at" (12.425), here with the person as object |
| βροτοῦ ἀνέρος ἔμβαλον εὐνῇ (18.85) | "cast you into the bed of a mortal man" | "put you in the bed of a mortal man" | "married you to", "gave you to"; the Greek says only "put into the bed" |
| αἴθ’ ὄφελες … ναίειν, Πηλεὺς δὲ … ἀγαγέσθαι ἄκοιτιν (18.86–87) | "If only you had stayed right there among the immortal women of the sea to dwell, and Peleus had taken a mortal wife" | "If only you had stayed right there, living among the immortal women of the sea, and Peleus had taken a mortal wife" | "Would that you had", "I wish" (the table's αἴθ’ ὄφελες is "If only", 1.415, 3.428); ἁλίῃσι "of the sea" taken as a noun, the sea-goddesses; ἄκοιτις "wife" (3.138 row) |
| πένθος ἐνὶ φρεσὶ μυρίον (18.88) | "countless grief in your wits" | "countless grief in your mind" | "boundless", "ten thousand"; μυρίος "countless" (2.468); φρένες "wits" in `l`, "mind" in `i`, as at 1.362 |
| παιδὸς ἀποφθιμένοιο (18.89, aorist of a death not yet come) | "for a child having perished" | "for a son who has perished" | "who is about to die", "who will perish" (state the future the Greek leaves as aorist); ἀποφθίνω "perish" |
| ἐπεὶ οὐδ’ ἐμὲ θυμὸς ἄνωγε ζώειν (18.90–91) | "since neither does my spirit bid me live" | "since my spirit does not bid me go on living" | "wish to live"; ἄνωγε "bids" (11.646 row), reserved |
| ἀπὸ θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ (18.92) | "lose his spirit" | "loses his life" | "breathe his last", "give up the ghost"; θυμός "spirit" in `l`, "life" in `i` (where it is the spirit that leaves the body) |
| ἕλωρα … ἀποτίσῃ (18.93) | "pay the price for the prey of Patroclus" | "pays the price for the prey he made of Patroclus" | "pay for the spoils of", "avenge" (hides the payment); ἕλωρ "prey" (13.208), ἀποτίνω "pay the price" (11.118) |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε Θέτις κατὰ δάκρυ χέουσα (18.94, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then in turn addressed Thetis, down a tear shedding" | "Then Thetis, shedding tears, spoke to him in turn" | "answered" (reserved for ἀμείβομαι), "weeping" (drops χέουσα); follows τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε Μενοιτίου ἄλκιμος υἱός (11.837) and κατὰ δάκρυ χέουσα (1.413) |
| ὠκύμορος δή μοι τέκος ἔσσεαι (18.95) | "Swift-doomed you will be, my child" | "My child, you will be swift to your doom" | "short-lived" (μινυνθάδιος), "doomed to die"; follows ὠκύμορος "swift to your doom" (1.417) |
| πότμος ἑτοῖμος (18.96) | "your doom is ready" | "your doom stands ready" | "fate" (reserved for μοῖρα), "death"; πότμος "doom" (4.170 row) |

Reused unchanged (no new row): the published lines at 18.1 (iliad-069), 18.5 (iliad-067, whole unit verbatim), 18.15 (iliad-067, first line only; same wording), 18.22 first line (iliad-114, with "Achilles" for "Hector" in `i`), 18.23 (odyssey-117, first line), 18.36 second line (iliad-004), 18.72 (odyssey-008, second line), 18.73 (iliad-004, 1.362, both units verbatim), 18.78 (iliad-004, whole unit verbatim); πόδας ταχύς "swift in feet / swift of foot" (the table's πόδας ὠκύς and 17.676); Μενοιτίου ἄλκιμος υἱός "Menoetius' sturdy son" (11.605, 16.307); κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ "Hector of the glancing helmet" (2.816, 3.324); κάρη κομόωντες Ἀχαιοί "the long-haired-of-head / long-haired Achaeans" (7.442); ἀγγελίη ἀλεγεινή "grievous news" (2.787); δαΐφρων "wise-hearted" (4.252); ἔπεα πτερόεντα "winged words" (1.201); πότνια μήτηρ "lady mother" (1.357); Τροίην ἐρίβωλον "rich-soiled Troy" (9.329); ἀγλαὰ δῶρα "splendid gifts" (ἀγλαός "splendid", 1.23); ἀτυζόμενοι "dazed with fear" (6.38); κλονέονται "thrown into confusion" (4.302, 5.8).

Departures from the Odyssey English: none. Line 18.23 first half and 18.72 second half reuse odyssey-117 and odyssey-008 verbatim.

Edition and numbering: nothing in 18.1–96 is bracketed, omitted or renumbered; the edition prints no quotation marks, so the speeches (6–14, 18–21, 52–64, 73–77, 79–93, 95–96) are marked by the `mark` field and by “ ” in the English layers only. The speech running into this part from iliad-115: none (iliad-115 ends at 17.761 on the narrator's own words, the fighting at the ditch not stopping).
